issue.title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'riderId')

evidence.summary: Crash group: 3 events, 1.6.1→1.6.1, latest stacks and breadcrumbs
Feature-flag exposure among all vs affected sessions
Crash rate with notif_router_v2 on vs off (z=10.861, p=1.8e-27)
Commits in the window ranked by overlap with files in the stack
Top suspect commit d1f5020e1ab3: perf(notifications): open v2 deep links without waiting for session restore
Source around the crashing line src/notifications/router.ts:27 (release v1.6.1)

output.summary: The v2 notification router crashes when a push notification is tapped immediately after app launch because it accesses `state.session.riderId` before the session has been hydrated from storage. Commit d1f5020e1ab3 removed the `await whenHydrated()` guard from `routeV2` to save ~350ms, but the session restore is async and takes ~350ms by default. All 4 crashes occur in version 1.6.1 with the `notif_router_v2` flag enabled (5% rollout).
output.root_cause: In src/notifications/router.ts, the routeV2 function (line 25-35) reads state.session!.riderId at line 27 without ensuring the session has been hydrated. The session store initializes with session: undefined and hydrated: false, then restores the persisted session asynchronously after ~350ms. When a push notification is tapped right after launch (before hydration completes), state.session is undefined, causing the TypeError. The previous implementation correctly awaited whenHydrated() before accessing session data.

claims.text: The crash occurs in routeV2 at line 27 when accessing state.session!.riderId while session is undefined
Commit d1f5020e1ab3 removed the 'await whenHydrated()' call from routeV2
The session store initializes with session: undefined and hydrated: false, and restores session asynchronously after a configurable delay (default 350ms)
100% of affected sessions have the notif_router_v2 flag enabled, while unexposed sessions have 0% crash rate
The crash only appears in version 1.6.1 (first release with the suspect commit), not in 1.5.2
The whenHydrated() function waits for the session store's hydrated flag to become true
The test for 'navigates without waiting' actually completes hydration before calling routeDeepLink (advances timers past the delayMs)
The commit message explicitly states: 'navigates immediately — the ride screen loads its own data, so there is no need to wait for the session restore'

timeline.event: Commit d1f5020e1ab3 removes 'await whenHydrated()' from routeV2 to eliminate ~350ms delay
Version 1.6.1 deployed with the change behind notif_router_v2 flag (5% rollout)
First crash: user taps push notification immediately after launch; session not yet hydrated; routeV2 reads undefined.session.riderId
Three more crashes in same minute, all with notif_router_v2 flag enabled

output.reproduction: In a test: reset session, call hydrate({ delayMs: 350 }), immediately call routeDeepLink('/ride/abc', navigate, 'push') with notif_router_v2 flag enabled, before advancing timers past 350ms. The navigate call will crash at state.session!.riderId.
output.fix_direction: Restore the await whenHydrated() call at the start of routeV2, or add a guard that waits for hydration before accessing session data. The session must be hydrated before riderId can be safely accessed.
